edit.description: `Predicate::ReachedFrom { roots, via }` joins the closed enum (:186). `roots` is a requirement name — the closure's roots are its satisfiers, named exactly as `Membership`'s `target` names its source set (:372), so it rides the `target` column and no second naming scheme appears. `via` is the field set DEGREE-FIELD-SET-FILTER landed on the shared `fields` column, which `Degree` (:382) already documents as `reached-from`'s too. `key()` (:696) answers `reached-from`; `ranges_over_selection` (:745) is true beside `degree`; `target()` (:764) and `documented_field()` (:812) are `None` (it names no one field — the `mention-reachable` precedent) and `declared_keys` (:865) skips it; `predicate_from_row` (:514) decodes the `target` + `fields` columns and never the `field` one, which carries only the synthesized label segment.

The set-predicate arms the variant rides: `judge` (:657) leaves it to the graph exactly as `degree` is left (:704), and the per-member arms at :301/:357/:405/:1354 list it with the other selection predicates. `inadmissibilities` (:177, `Degree`'s own vacuity cases at :502) gains its two, both by standing precedent: an empty `roots` names no requirement to root from (`membership`'s rule verbatim), and an empty `via` follows no field — the closure would be the root set, so every non-root member fires, the false positive a directionless `degree` is already refused for.

New `reached_from` beside `degree` (:417), taking the same `(&[Selection], &[ResolvedEdge], &[ResolvedEdge], &BTreeMap<&str, &[Features]>)`. Opt-in through `any_clause_of` (:315), so a corpus declaring no such clause does no closure work. Per clause: the roots are the members of the `Selector::OptIn(roots)` selection — read off the same `selections` slice `engine::out_of_set` reads for `membership`, not a second satisfier walk — then a forward BFS over the via-filtered adjacency, reusing the per-clause field filter DEGREE-FIELD-SET-FILTER factored out rather than re-filtering. A visited set makes the closure well-defined over cycles; a root holds trivially by construction. One diagnostic per selected member outside the closure, at the clause's own severity and carrying its guidance (`degree` :608 is the shape), naming the roots requirement and the via set.

Wire `graph::reached_from` after the `degree` call (:593), reading the hoisted `resolved_edges` (:575) and `mention_edges` the two graph judges around it already share, plus the one `selections` list that holds the opt-in, by-kind and root bindings (:505-:517) — the roots resolve off it, so no new corpus walk enters the gate.

`ClauseRow::target`'s doc (:3800) widens to two owners — `membership`'s allowed-set source and `reached-from`'s roots requirement — and `to_table` (:4766) / `from_table` (:4843) write and read it for either predicate. The via set needs no column of its own: it is the `fields` column (:3813) DEGREE-FIELD-SET-FILTER added, whose doc already names this predicate as its second consumer. Riding this file's opening: `EmitOwnedEntry::path`'s doc (:3451) still points at `install::matches_projection`, renamed `matched_projection` at 60775513 (`install.rs:992`).

The keystroke-schema skip arm (:110-:131, where `mention-reachable`, `degree` and `reachable` already sit): a graph-scope predicate constrains no field of a document, so it contributes nothing to an emitted JSON Schema.

The judge's cases beside the `degree` ones: a member the roots reach transitively passes and an unlinked one fires; a root holds trivially; a cycle inside the closure terminates and changes no verdict; a via set naming one field ignores another field's arcs; a mention or import field counts only where the via set names it; and a selection with no `reached-from` clause produces no finding.
The declaration round trip: a `reached-from` row survives write→read with its `target` and `fields` columns intact, and lifts back into the same predicate.

`covered_rule`'s exhaustive `Predicate` match (:165-:188) — a new variant is a compile error until it joins the schema-silent arm, which is the correct verdict: a graph-scope predicate measures no manifest rule.

edit.description: `orderedFields` (:495) returns `[...head, ...typed, ...residueFields(init)]` with no key check and `residueFields` (:504) key-sorts the bag blind, so a residue key the surface also types is projected twice — residue last, and the engine's writer collects the pair list into a map (`drift.rs:2521`), so the untyped value wins silently. Both halves of the partition are in hand at that one call, which is where the refusal belongs; `RESERVED_LEAF` (:424) is the shape precedent — a framework name refused at the constructor, never resolved. A compile-time narrowing of the bag's key type against `keyof T` is the stronger front door where it types cleanly, but cannot be the only half: the erased caller reaches the same splice.

`Settings`' and `SettingsLocal`'s `residue?: Readonly<Record<string, unknown>>` declarations (`SettingsLocal`'s at :1234) take whatever narrowed bag type `kind.ts` exports, and their docs state the partition `builtins.md` draws: a key this surface types is spelled as that field, never here.
Export the bag type if the narrowing lands as one — a custom kind's surface declaring `residue?` is authored outside this package, and an unexported type ships nowhere.

The refusal: a member init spelling a typed key inside `residue` is rejected — `@ts-expect-error` for the compile-time half (the suite's `tsc -p` pass fails on a directive that stops firing) and a thrown-refusal assertion for the erased one.
Pin that no projection can carry one key twice, and that the non-colliding case is untouched: a residue key the surface does not type still splices flat, key-sorted, after the typed fields.

summary: The residue bag silently overrides a typed field: the splice takes no collision check, so a residue key the surface also types projects the untyped value and drops the typed one.

acceptance: `pnpm --dir sdk test` (strict `tsc` + `node --test`) green. `cargo test` is untouched — the wire is unchanged and no lock row moves; the engine's field-list-to-map collect stays the writer's, since the partition is the authoring surface's to hold.
